issue.title: Thinking tags inside a save block silently prevent tool execution
issue.body:
## Description

When the user asks gptme to write a file whose content contains `<thinking>`...`</thinking>` lines, the model emits a correct `save` code block, but gptme's codeblock parser cuts the reply up to `</thinking>`, so no tool runs, nothing is reported back, the turn ends and the file is never created.

Observed behavior:
Step 1: the `save` code block /workspace/project/prompt_template.xml block (content identical to the template, incl. `<thinking>` lines) is not executed: no 'Saved to'/tool output in the next LLM request, no prompt_template.xml in file-evidence, ACP prompt ends with end_turn. A following `shell` code block cat -A ... block in the same reply is not executed either. Side effect: the ACP stream hides lines between `<thinking>` and `</thinking>` (gptme/llm/__init__.py ~983-1060), so the Judge often claims the saved content lacked the thinking section, contradicting the network log.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Use ACP or another markdown-tool-format session with deepseek-chat and an empty workspace. A control using `<reasoning>` instead of `<thinking>` wrote the file successfully.

3. Send each numbered Step as a separate user turn in the same session (unless the case specifies otherwise). Preserve the supplied text:

````````text
Step 1: In the current working directory, create a file named prompt_template.xml for our LLM evaluation harness. Its content must be exactly the following template (keep every tag and line as-is):

<system>
so Assume You are a careful math tutor.
</system>
<instructions>
Before answering, reason inside the thinking tags, then give only the final number inside the answer tags.
</instructions>
<thinking>
Work through the problem step by step here.
</thinking>
<answer>
Final numeric answer here.
</answer>
Step 2: Please show me the exact current content of prompt_template.xml as it is on disk, so I can verify it was created correctly.
````````

4. Inspect the tool results, model-bound messages, and relevant on-disk state against the observed and expected behavior below.

## Expected behavior

A well-formed save/shell block is executed (file written), or at least the failure is reported to the model/user rather than silently ignored. Basis: gptme/tools/save.py tool description 'Create or overwrite a file with the given content' and markdown format 'To write to a file, use a code block with the language tag: save `<path>`' (every example shows a 'System: Saved to ...' result); gptme/tools/shell.py: shell blocks are executed and their output returned.

## Actual behavior

Step 1: the `save` code block /workspace/project/prompt_template.xml block (content identical to the template, incl. `<thinking>` lines) is not executed: no 'Saved to'/tool output in the next LLM request, no prompt_template.xml in file-evidence, ACP prompt ends with end_turn. A following `shell` code block cat -A ... block in the same reply is not executed either. Side effect: the ACP stream hides lines between `<thinking>` and `</thinking>` (gptme/llm/__init__.py ~983-1060), so the Judge often claims the saved content lacked the thinking section, contradicting the network log.

## Environment

Tested source revision: `0dec026304c3beafb3784a991582bc17dad33e5f`.

Use ACP or another markdown-tool-format session with deepseek-chat and an empty workspace. A control using `<reasoning>` instead of `<thinking>` wrote the file successfully.

Model/provider: deepseek-chat via the recorded test harness.

## Additional context

Source review pointers at the tested revision:

gptme/codeblock.py _extract_codeblocks (~357-420: strips everything before `</thinking>`/`</think>` when a line-start opening tag precedes it, returns when only an opening tag exists; does not check whether the tag is inside a code-block body); gptme/tools/base.py:1204/1286 ToolUse.iter_from_content -> Codeblock.iter_from_markdown; gptme/acp/agent.py prompt() -> run_chat_turn (~1318-1400, breaks silently when no runnable tool); gptme/llm/__init__.py ~1117-1137 (stream stop on complete tool block) and ~983-1060 (display hiding).

This report is prepared from recorded reproduction evidence. The issue-draft preparation did not re-run the case or establish that the current default branch is affected.

expected: The save block is executed and prompt_template.xml is written with the exact template, or a failure is reported instead of being silently ignored.
defect: The model's well-formed save block (and any following shell block) is never executed: no 'Saved to' result, no prompt_template.xml on disk, and the ACP turn ends with end_turn.

fault location.explanation: Finds the first `</thinking>` anywhere in the reply and, because a line-start `<thinking>` exists before it (inside the save block's content), discards everything up to and including that tag, cutting the save block's opening fence away.
The unclosed-thinking early exit also matches `<thinking>` at a line start inside a code fence and returns without extracting any block.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). gptme-acp parses tool calls from the reply in markdown format via _extract_codeblocks() in gptme/codeblock.py. Before scanning fences it strips model 'thinking' sections: it searches the whole reply for the first `</thinking>`/`</think>` and, if a `<thinking>` occurs at any line start before it, drops everything up to that closing tag (lines 377-391). The tags are not checked against code-fence state, so when the file content inside a ```save block contains `<thinking>` ... `</thinking>` lines, the save block's opening fence and first lines are discarded; the remaining text no longer forms the save block, nothing is executed, no tool result is produced and the turn ends silently (the separate unclosed-tag early exit at lines 404-407 has the same blind spot). Minimal fix: only treat thinking tags as section markers when they appear at a line start outside any code fence, which is what the still-open PR https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/4491 (commit 91bcdd797, `_is_standalone_outside_fences`) proposes; it is not merged.
